questions.question: Many investors wait until they have owned an investment for more than one year before selling it because

options.B: long-term gains often get lower tax rates.
options.C: investments can't legally be sold within a year.

questions.explanation: Long-term gains often get lower tax rates. U.S. tax law usually taxes profits on investments held more than one year, called long-term capital gains, at lower rates than profits on investments held a year or less, which are taxed like ordinary income. Investments can be sold at any time, short-term gains are taxed, and long-term gains are often taxed, just at lower rates. Timing sales is one legal way to reduce taxes, but investors should also consider whether holding longer makes sense for the investment itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason restaurants carry liability insurance even when they follow every health rule:

options.A: Health rules require them to close
options.B: Customers might still sue over an illness

questions.explanation: Customers might still sue over an illness. Even a careful restaurant can face a customer who claims a meal made him or her sick, and defending a lawsuit is expensive whether or not the claim succeeds. Liability insurance covers legal costs and any damages owed. Health rules don't require restaurants to close, insurance can't prevent illness, and it doesn't replace inspections by health departments. Many landlords and event organizers require proof of liability insurance before a restaurant can lease space or cater an event.

questions.question: Harbor Point Credit Union's CRM data shows that members who use three or more of its products are much less likely to leave than members who use only one. How might the credit union best use this information?

options.A: Close the accounts of single-product members
options.B: Charge higher monthly fees to its most loyal members
options.D: Stop collecting data about its members

questions.explanation: Offer single-product members fitting services. The data suggests that members with several products are more loyal, so the credit union can offer single-product members services that fit their needs, such as a savings account, credit card or car loan. Closing accounts would lose members, stopping data collection would remove useful insight, and charging loyal members more would push them away. Using CRM data this way is called cross-selling, and it works best when offers genuinely benefit the customer rather than simply adding products they don't need.

questions.question: When a client asks a financial advisor about an investment the advisor doesn't fully understand, the advisor should

options.B: steer the client to another product.
options.D: describe it as a guaranteed return.

questions.explanation: Research it before giving advice. Advisors have a responsibility to give advice based on knowledge, not guesses. Researching the investment, or referring the client to a specialist, protects the client and the advisor's reputation. Recommending something to look knowledgeable, calling it guaranteed or steering the client away without explanation could lead to poor decisions and may break industry rules. Being honest about the limits of one's knowledge builds trust, and clients generally appreciate an advisor who says, "Let me look into that and get back to you."

questions.question: A restaurant owner estimates next month's sales from current reservations and last year's results. She mainly uses this forecast to

options.A: plan food orders and staff schedules.

questions.explanation: Plan food orders and staff schedules. A sales forecast predicts how busy the restaurant will be, so the owner can order enough food without waste and schedule the right number of servers and cooks. Recording last month's expenses is bookkeeping about the past, not planning. Employees' taxes are based on actual wages, and competitors' prices don't come from a sales forecast. Budgets built on realistic forecasts help small businesses avoid two expensive problems: running out of supplies on busy nights and paying staff to stand around on slow ones.

questions.question: When investors expect a recession, many move money from stocks into government bonds. They do this mainly because government bonds are viewed as
questions.explanation: Safer during economic downturns. During a recession, company profits often fall and stock prices can drop sharply, so investors look for safer places to keep their money. Government bonds are backed by the government's ability to collect taxes, making default unlikely. Bonds aren't certain to double, they do pay interest, and they are generally considered less risky than stocks, not more. This shift, often called a flight to safety, can push bond prices up and interest rates down when economic news turns negative.

questions.question: Members of Peak Fitness Gym report a broken treadmill, but employees leave it in use for two weeks without fixing it or posting a warning. A member is then injured on it. Which legal concept would most likely apply?
questions.explanation: Negligence. Negligence is a failure to take reasonable care that results in harm to someone. The gym knew the treadmill was broken and neither fixed it nor warned members, so it could be held responsible for the injury. Copyright infringement involves copying creative work. Breach of contract involves breaking an agreement's terms, which isn't the main issue here. Product tampering means deliberately altering a product. Businesses reduce this risk with regular inspections, quick repairs and clear warning signs.

questions.question: An insurance company serves as a financial institution mainly by

options.A: setting the prices of listed stocks.
options.C: printing and issuing the nation's currency.
options.D: pooling premiums to pay members' losses.

questions.explanation: Pooling premiums to pay members' losses. Insurance companies collect premiums from many policyholders and use that pool to pay the losses of the few who file claims, spreading risk across a large group. They also invest the premiums, which makes them major participants in financial markets. Currency is issued by the government, not insurers. Stock prices are set by buyers and sellers in the market, and Congress approves the federal budget. Insurers, banks and investment firms together make up the financial services industry.

questions.question: A small business buys equipment that it will use for ten years. Under tax rules, the cost is usually

options.A: added to the business's taxable income.
options.C: ignored because it is a business asset.
options.D: deducted twice in the year of purchase.

questions.explanation: Deducted over time as depreciation. Long-lasting assets lose value as they are used, so tax rules generally let businesses deduct their cost gradually over their useful life through depreciation. Deducting it twice would be improper, and the purchase reduces rather than increases taxable income. The cost isn't ignored, because depreciation is a legitimate business expense. Some tax rules let small businesses deduct more of the cost in the first year, which is why owners often work with accountants when making large purchases.

questions.question: A lender reviewing a business's balance sheet sees that its liabilities are much larger than its assets. This analysis suggests the business has
questions.explanation: High financial risk. When a business owes far more than it owns, its equity is negative, and it may struggle to repay debts if sales fall. Lenders treat this as high financial risk and may deny a loan or charge a higher rate. Strong liquidity would mean plenty of cash or assets that convert quickly to cash, profitability is measured on the income statement, and credit history comes from past payment records. Lenders usually combine the balance sheet with income and cash flow information before deciding.

options.A: are legally guaranteed to be correct.

questions.explanation: May be inaccurate or biased. Anyone can post in an online forum, and some posters exaggerate or spread false information to push a stock's price up or down for their own profit. Forum posts aren't reviewed by regulators, carry no legal guarantee and cover many kinds of investments, not just government bonds. Investors should check claims against reliable sources, such as company filings and established financial news. Regulators have charged people who used social media to promote stocks they secretly planned to sell.

questions.question: When the U.S. dollar strengthens against other currencies, U.S. companies that sell heavily overseas may see their stock prices fall because

options.A: their goods cost more for foreign buyers.
options.D: foreign customers earn more U.S. dollars.

questions.explanation: Their goods cost more for foreign buyers. A stronger dollar means foreign buyers must spend more of their own currency to buy U.S. goods, which can reduce overseas sales and the value of profits earned abroad. Investors who expect lower earnings may sell the stock. Foreign customers don't earn more dollars when the dollar strengthens, foreign interest rates don't rise automatically, and U.S. production costs remain. Exchange rates are one of several economic factors, along with interest rates and inflation, that investors watch when judging companies with large international sales.

questions.question: Sparrow Design budgeted $12,000 for marketing this quarter. By the end of the second month it had spent $10,500, mostly because a trade show cost more than expected. What is the best budgeting decision for the final month?

options.B: Replace the budget with a new one next year

questions.explanation: Limit spending to the remaining $1,500. Sparrow has $12,000 - $10,500 = $1,500 left, so the best choice is to limit the final month's spending to that amount and look for low-cost activities. Spending another $12,000 would double the budget. Stopping tracking hides the problem, and waiting until next year to replace the budget does nothing about this quarter. Comparing actual spending with the budget during the quarter, not just at the end, is what gives managers time to adjust before an overrun becomes serious.

questions.question: Which of the following increases the future value of money saved today:
questions.explanation: A higher interest rate. Future value depends on the amount saved, the interest rate and the length of time the money grows. A higher interest rate means each year's growth is larger, so the money is worth more in the future. A shorter time period gives interest less time to compound, fewer deposits mean less money earning interest, and fees reduce the balance. Starting to save early is often more powerful than saving larger amounts later, because compounding needs time.

questions.question: A company's net income was $50,000 on net sales of $500,000. What is its net profit margin?
questions.explanation: 10%. Net profit margin equals net income divided by net sales: $50,000 / $500,000 = 0.10, or 10%. The company keeps 10 cents of profit from every dollar of sales. An answer of 50% comes from misplacing the decimal, 1% from moving it the other way, and 25% doesn't come from these numbers. Profit margins vary widely by industry; grocery stores often earn only a few cents per dollar, while software companies can earn far more.

questions.question: An insurance company offers discounts to homeowners who install sensors that detect water leaks and send alerts to their phones. How does this help the insurer manage risk?

options.A: Homeowners must buy a second policy
options.B: Every customer's premium will rise each year
options.C: The insurer no longer pays water claims
options.D: Owners can stop leaks before damage spreads

questions.explanation: Owners can stop leaks before damage spreads. Water damage is one of the most common and expensive home insurance claims. A sensor that alerts the homeowner early lets him or her shut off the water before a small leak ruins floors and walls, so claims become smaller and less frequent. The program uses discounts, not higher premiums, and the insurer still pays covered claims. No second policy is needed. Insurers increasingly use connected devices to prevent losses rather than simply paying for them after they occur.

questions.question: A company's chief financial officer tells the accounting team to spread a large one-time loss over several years as an ordinary expense so this year's profit looks better to investors. The team knows accounting rules require the loss to be reported now. Several team members worry about their jobs if they refuse. What is the most ethical response?

options.A: Report the loss in a footnote only
options.B: Report the loss correctly and raise the concern
options.C: Follow the request because the CFO is in charge
options.D: Delay reporting the loss until next year

questions.explanation: Report the loss correctly and raise the concern. Financial statements must follow accounting rules, and hiding or spreading out a loss to mislead investors is fraud, no matter who asks. The team should record the loss correctly and raise the concern, going to the audit committee or an ethics hotline if needed. Following the CFO's request, delaying the loss or burying it in a footnote all mislead investors. Laws such as the Sarbanes-Oxley Act protect employees who report accounting fraud from retaliation, which addresses the team's worry about their jobs.

questions.question: Before approving a first credit card for Jada, a college sophomore with no credit history, Crestline Bank reviews her paystubs from a part-time job she has held for 18 months and statements showing her savings account grew from $400 to $2,300 over two years. She has never missed a rent payment to her roommate. Why does the bank review these items?

options.B: To confirm she has a cosigner
options.C: To judge her ability to manage money
options.D: To set the card's annual percentage rate by law

questions.explanation: To judge her ability to manage money. Without a credit history, the bank needs other evidence that the student can repay what she borrows. Steady income shows she can make payments, and a growing savings balance shows she lives within her means. The bank sets the rate based on its own policies and her risk, not a legal formula tied to these items. Income and savings don't prove she has a cosigner or show her enrollment. Many first-time borrowers start with a student or secured card to build a credit history.

questions.question: Which of the following finance professionals examines a company's records to make sure its financial statements are accurate:
questions.explanation: Auditor. Auditors review a company's records, transactions and controls to confirm that its financial statements are accurate and follow accounting rules. A loan officer evaluates applications and decides whether borrowers qualify for loans. An insurance underwriter judges how risky an applicant is and sets the terms of a policy. A mortgage broker connects home buyers with lenders. Auditing careers include internal auditors, who work for one company, and external auditors, who work for accounting firms and review many clients each year.

questions.question: Two regional banks merge and then close 15 branches that were within a mile of each other. The main reason for closing these branches is to
questions.explanation: Reduce duplicate operating costs. After a merger, a bank often has two branches serving the same neighborhood, so it pays rent, utilities and staff twice for the same customers. Closing one of each pair cuts these duplicate costs, which is a major reason banks merge. Closing branches doesn't attract customers or add employees, and the merged bank remains under government oversight. Banks usually keep the branch with the better location and move accounts so customers can continue banking nearby.

questions.question: A manufacturer learns that a small number of its space heaters may overheat. A recall would be expensive, and no one has been hurt yet. Which choice reflects ethical risk management?

options.A: Warn customers and offer a repair

questions.explanation: Warn customers and offer a repair. Ethical risk management puts customer safety ahead of short-term cost. Warning customers and offering a repair reduces the chance of fires and injuries, and it also protects the company from lawsuits and damage to its reputation. Waiting for an injury, fixing only future models or removing warnings leaves customers exposed to a known danger. Companies are also legally required to report certain product hazards to the Consumer Product Safety Commission, which can order recalls.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of having a mentor early in a finance career:
questions.explanation: Learning from someone's experience. A mentor is an experienced professional who shares advice, explains how the industry works and helps a newer employee avoid common mistakes. That guidance can speed up learning and open doors to new contacts. A mentor can't guarantee promotions, doesn't replace the training an employer requires, and doesn't excuse anyone from performance reviews. Many finance firms run formal mentoring programs because employees with mentors often build skills faster and stay with the company longer.

questions.question: A stock is trading at $60 per share, and the company earned $4 per share last year. What is its price-to-earnings ratio?
questions.explanation: 15. The P/E ratio equals the share price divided by earnings per share: $60 / $4 = 15. Investors are paying $15 for every $1 of annual earnings. Multiplying instead of dividing gives 240, adding the numbers gives 64, and subtracting them gives 56. A P/E of 15 is close to the long-term average for many large U.S. stocks, but whether it is high or low depends on the company's growth prospects and how it compares with similar companies.

questions.question: A bank that refuses to approve home loans in certain neighborhoods mainly because of the residents' race is violating
questions.explanation: Fair lending laws. Fair lending laws, such as the Fair Housing Act and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, make it illegal to deny credit or offer worse terms based on race and other protected characteristics. Refusing loans in neighborhoods because of residents' race is a practice known as redlining. Truth-in-advertising laws cover misleading ads, securities registration laws cover the sale of stocks and bonds, and workplace safety laws protect employees. Regulators can fine banks that discriminate and require them to make up for the harm.

questions.question: The owner of Rise & Shine Bakery compares register reports with bank deposit slips and finds that, for six weeks, recorded cash sales have been $50 to $200 higher than the cash deposited each day. The same cashier counts the drawer, prepares the deposit and takes it to the bank. Which internal control would best address this problem?

options.A: Deposits are made once a month
options.B: A second person verifies each deposit
options.D: Cashiers keep their own sales records

questions.explanation: A second person verifies each deposit. Separating duties so that one person counts the cash and another verifies the deposit makes it much harder to take money without being noticed, and it catches honest counting errors too. Letting cashiers take deposits home or keep their own records gives one person too much control, and monthly deposits leave large amounts of cash on site for weeks. Comparing register reports with bank deposits every day, as the owner should now do, is a basic control for any business that handles cash.

options.B: They need funds for a short period
options.C: They want to avoid paying interest

questions.explanation: They need funds for a short period. The money market is where organizations borrow and lend for short periods, usually less than a year, through instruments such as Treasury bills and commercial paper. A business might use it to cover payroll while waiting for customers to pay. Buying ownership shares happens in the stock market, a part of the capital market. Long-term projects, such as 30-year construction, are funded in the capital market. Money-market borrowers still pay interest, though usually at lower rates than long-term loans.

questions.explanation: An internal control. Internal controls are policies and procedures a business creates to protect its assets and make sure records are accurate. questions.question: An insurance company that denies valid claims to increase its profits is acting unethically because it
questions.explanation: Breaks its promise to policyholders. An insurance policy is a promise to pay covered losses in exchange for premiums. questions.question: The people outside a company who rely most on its financial-information management function are usually

questions.question: Priya, a new financial analyst, attends an industry networking event but spends the evening talking only with two coworkers she already knows. Which approach would have better built her professional network?

options.C: Meeting new people and following up

questions.question: It is unethical for an accountant to use a client's confidential financial information to make personal investments because it

options.A: makes the client's financial statements more accurate.
options.B: helps the client earn a higher return.

options.A: eliminate the need for a budget.

questions.question: Kestrel Outdoor Gear grew from one store to nine in three years. Its owner still records every sale and expense in one spreadsheet that only she can open, and she prepares reports only when the bank asks for them. options.D: A larger advertising budget for each store

questions.question: As part of enterprise risk management, a hospital's leaders decide they will accept small financial risks to try new services but no risks that could harm patient safety. This decision describes the hospital's
questions.explanation: Risk appetite. Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organization is willing to accept to reach its goals. The hospital accepts some financial risk but none involving patient safety, which guides future decisions. Risk transfer shifts a risk to someone else, often through insurance. questions.question: Malcolm deposits $1,000 in an account that pays 10% simple interest per year. How much interest will he earn after three years?
questions.explanation: $300. Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, so the interest is the same each year, while compound interest grows because interest is earned on past interest.

questions.question: Which financial ratio would best help a manager judge how much of each sales dollar a company keeps as profit:
questions.explanation: Net profit margin. Net profit margin divides net income by net sales, showing the share of each sales dollar left as profit after all expenses. The current ratio compares current assets with current liabilities to measure short-term liquidity. The debt-to-equity ratio shows how much a company relies on borrowing, and inventory turnover shows how quickly inventory sells. questions.question: Lumière Housewares, a U.S. company, owns a French subsidiary that earned 1 million euros in profit this year. options.B: It no longer has to be reported

The amount can't stay the same because exchange rates changed, and foreign profits must still be reported. Companies often use hedging tools, such as forward contracts, to reduce the effect of exchange-rate swings on their results.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of paying suppliers through electronic payment systems:

Many small businesses now pay most suppliers electronically for these reasons.

questions.question: A bank's CRM system can help make sure no customer request is forgotten by
questions.explanation: Sending task reminders to employees. Annual reports, stock prices and printed statements involve the bank's finances or routine mailings rather than tracking individual customer requests. Prompt follow-up is one of the main ways banks build loyalty, because customers who have to repeat a request several times are much more likely to move their accounts elsewhere.

performanceIndicator.text: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology

questions.question: A U.S. retirement fund invests part of its money in companies in Europe and Asia. The fund is mainly trying to

options.C: support only businesses based in the U.S.

questions.explanation: Spread risk across economies. Economies don't always rise and fall together, so owning companies in several regions can reduce the impact of a downturn in any single country. This is international diversification. No strategy avoids all risk, and investing abroad actually adds currency risk rather than avoiding it. Supporting only U.S. businesses would mean keeping all the money at home. Many retirement plans include international funds so that savers benefit from growth in other parts of the world.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of financial globalization

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how a finance professional should handle clients' personal information:

options.A: Leaving client files on a shared desk
options.B: Using client names in public success stories
options.C: Sharing it only as law and policy permit

questions.explanation: Sharing it only as law and policy permit. Finance professionals must keep client information private and share it only when laws and company policies allow, such as with regulators or a client's authorized representative. Posting client stories with names, discussing accounts with friends and leaving files where others can see them all expose private information without permission. These breaches can harm clients through identity theft and can lead to fines and lost jobs. Many firms require employees to complete privacy training every year.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services

questions.question: Financial firms collect a great deal of personal information about customers. Which of the following is the main reason they must follow strict rules about how they share it:

options.A: Privacy laws limit sharing of customer data
options.B: Customers legally own the firm's computers
options.C: The information has no value to the firm
options.D: Sharing any data is always illegal

questions.explanation: Privacy laws limit sharing of customer data. Financial privacy laws, such as the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, require firms to explain how they use customer information, protect it and, in many cases, let customers opt out of certain sharing. The information is valuable to firms, which is exactly why rules limit its use. Customers don't own a firm's computers, and sharing is not always illegal: firms may share data with regulators or service providers under specific conditions. Firms that mishandle customer data can face fines, lawsuits and a serious loss of trust.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss legal considerations in the finance industry

questions.question: A farmer sells a contract agreeing to deliver corn at a set price in six months to protect against falling corn prices. This transaction takes place in the
questions.explanation: Futures market. A futures market trades contracts to buy or sell a commodity, such as corn, at a set price on a future date. Farmers use futures to lock in prices and reduce the risk of a price drop before harvest. The primary stock market is where companies first sell new shares, the money market handles short-term borrowing, and the bond market trades long-term debt. Food processors use the same futures markets to protect themselves against rising prices, so both sides reduce their risk.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of financial markets (e.g., money market, capital market, insurance market, commodities markets, etc.)

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of enterprise risk management compared with managing risks department by department:
questions.explanation: Leaders see how risks connect. Enterprise risk management looks at all of an organization's risks together, so leaders can see how a problem in one area, such as a supplier failure, could affect sales, finances and reputation. Department-by-department management can miss these connections. ERM encourages departments to share risk information, makes risk management more organized rather than unnecessary, and still uses insurance to transfer some risks. Many large companies have a chief risk officer who leads ERM efforts. ERM reports usually go to the board of directors as well as senior managers.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of enterprise risk management (ERM)

questions.question: Elena is a high school senior who wants a finance career but isn't sure which area suits her. Which step would best help her explore her options before choosing a college major?

options.B: Picking the job with the highest salary
options.C: Job shadowing in several finance roles
options.D: Applying only to the largest local banks

questions.explanation: Job shadowing in several finance roles. Job shadowing lets Elena watch professionals such as analysts, bankers and accountants at work, so she can compare the daily tasks of different roles before committing to a major. Choosing by salary alone ignores whether she would enjoy or be good at the work. Applying only to large banks narrows her view to one part of the industry. Waiting until after graduation means she may pick a major that doesn't fit. Informational interviews and internships are other low-risk ways to test a career path.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss employment opportunities in the finance industry
